exposure: Robson's classification groups (maternal parity, previous uterine scar, fetal presentation, gestational age, onset of labor)
cohort: The study included 3176 women who underwent caesarean section at a rural teaching hospital.
finding: Pregnant women with prior uterine scars (Robson's Group 5) contribute most significantly to caesarean section rates.
mod_finding: The most common group contributing to caesarean section rates was Group 5 (multiparous women with at least one previous uterine scar, with single cephalic pregnancy, >=37 weeks gestation), followed by Group 2 (nulliparous women with single cephalic pregnancy, >37 weeks gestation, who either had labour induced or were delivered by caesarean section before labour).
gest_age: Gestational age >=37 weeks was a criterion for classification into certain Robson's groups, specifically Group 5 and Group 2.
